verdicts.note: Cached roll calls confirm Yea on ESSB 6346 (51-46), ESSB 5813 and ESHB 2081. The cached about page reads 'she fought and voted for the Millionaires' Tax' [S3], and GetLegislation confirms she is prime sponsor of HB 2626. Several independent taxes sources support +2 high.

Cached home page has 'building more homes of every type ... More supply means more options' next to 'stronger renter protections' [S2]. Add the EHB 1217 Yea [S10] and the HB 1763 sponsorship [S19] and she leans pole_b with real supply language, so +1. The record votes and sponsorship support high.

The only evidence is the PDC top-contributor list [S22]. It confirms $2,400 each from Regence, Genentech and Puget Sound Energy, but DaVita gave $2,200, not $2,400 as the basis says. Contributor names alone do not show which gifts came from PACs. Accepting contributions is behaviour, not a stated position on PAC money, term limits, dark money or RCV. The dossier has no statement from her on structural reform. Other wave refutations dropped fundraising-only reform scores to low (King's 'fundraising lead ... not positions on PAC money'; Strickland). Keep the direction at low.

GetLegislation confirms she is prime sponsor of HB 1445, 'Developing the Washington health trust' [S15], the universal-coverage vehicle. Her opponent's complaint that the bill stalled in committee does not change her stated direction. Sponsorship plus repeated website statements [S2][S3] support high.

Prime sponsor of HB 2657, the abortion savings program (confirmed in the cached GetLegislation record) [S17]. Planned Parenthood Votes NW endorsement confirmed on the cached endorsements page [S4]. Listed No on I-638 [S20]. The Urbanist calls her 'a champion for reproductive rights' [S23]. Record plus a stated stance supports high.
Cached roll calls confirm Yea on ESHB 1296 third reading and on Senate-amended final passage, and Nay on the Republican amendments. Also No on I-1 [S20]. Pole_b on the record.

Cached questionnaire [S5]: 'The platform on which I am running is heavily reliant on tax restructuring', 'personally champion ... a 2% Financial Intangibles Tax on asset portfolios exceeding $100 million', and a Land Value Tax. His website repeats the land value tax [S2]. Calling ESSB 6346 'performative' is a prediction about the courts, not opposition to taxing wealth. Repeated explicit statements support high.

Cached home page: 'Restrict annual rent increases to the rate of inflation, with no exemptions' and 'Repealing the Rent Control Ban (RCW 35.21.830)' [S2]. The questionnaire adds right to counsel [S5]. Fully pole_b, stated repeatedly.

Cached sources confirm 'The legislature must divest from the prison-industrial complex' and 'a full decriminalization of drug use' [S5], and that he 'will also propose to remove all SROs from schools' [S4].

This is zoning and preemption evidence, which belongs to local-control, and none of it is school governance. 'State preemption must be massively expanded' [S5] is explicit pole_b. It is offset in part by his call to restore local rent-control authority [S2], so +1 medium is a fair net.

His sources say 'corporate PAC-free' [S5] and that he 'wholly rejects corporate PACs and lobbying money' [S2], not all PAC money as the highlight implies. He also makes limits on corporate political spending and public election vouchers his top priority [S5]. Repeated explicit pole_b statements support +2 high.
Cached questionnaire: 'Do you support universal healthcare ... ? Unequivocally' and support for the Washington Health Trust [S5]. His website backs single-payer [S2].

There are only two pieces: the Stonewall Democrats endorsement [S2] and his listing as opposing I-638 [S7]. That is thin, and +1 medium already reflects it. The I-638 listing is his own public stance, not just a group's endorsement of him.

Rests on one item: his listing on the No-on-I-1 endorser page [S7]. That is a stance he took, not a third party endorsing him, so it counts as a single clear statement: +1 medium. His charter-school moratorium and levy-decoupling planks [S4] are school finance and choice, not notification or opt-out rights. Correctly left out.
